stem:
Kiara compares two litters of the same dog breed. The pups look like their parents but are not identical to them or to each other. Parents pass instructions to offspring, and small changes in those instructions can create differences.

Which claims correctly describe what reproduction does? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Reproduction keeps each type of organism from disappearing by passing instructions from parents to offspring.
Reproduction is the same as growth, so instructions never pass from parents to offspring.
Small changes in the instructions can create variation that may help survival when conditions change.
Variation erases continuity, so reproduction cannot keep a type of organism going.

teacher.key_rationale: Reproduction sustains continuity by passing instructions and can create helpful variation. Treating reproduction as mere growth, or saying variation blocks continuity, misses that hinge.
